headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and capability conflict; data leakage and cascading errors are also material because Haystack can use MCP/egress and Windsurf can read/write the same local files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, while Windsurf exposes clipboard, workspace files, and MCP servers. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests MCP or API content from a source Windsurf can write to the workspace or clipboard, then prompt injection is possible.
IF Windsurf parses workspace or clipboard content as instructions, then attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Restrict Haystack MCP endpoints to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
Use separate workspaces or directories for each agent.
Add a manual review step before Windsurf executes instructions derived from Haystack output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and uses MCP/REST APIs; Windsurf reads and writes workspace files and handles model provider keys. If they share a local workspace, sensitive source code or open files can flow into Haystack’s outbound requests or Windsurf’s context. The profiles show the necessary surfaces, but not a guaranteed leak path, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local workspace, then file contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to external APIs, then workspace data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Place the agents in separate directories.
Disable or narrow Haystack outbound API destinations.
Avoid opening secrets or private code in Windsurf while Haystack is active.
Rotate any keys stored in the shared workspace if exposure is suspected.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can read/write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress. Windsurf’s concurrency model explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, so simultaneous writes to the same repo can race and corrupt git or files. Because both agents have overlapping mutable access by default, the conflict is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, then concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Haystack also mutates shared files, then state corruption becomes likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone.
Pause one agent before the other writes git state.
Disable Windsurf auto-execute for shared repositories.
Use a lock file or single-writer workflow for edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can generate retrieved facts through MCP/REST, and Windsurf can act on workspace content and execute shell commands. If Windsurf treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commands. The profiles support the pathway, but Windsurf also has approval-per-command by default, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Haystack output as a source of truth without verification, then incorrect facts can propagate into edits or commands.
IF Haystack returns stale or hallucinated retrieval results, then Windsurf may operationalize them.
mitigations: Require a human check before acting on Haystack-derived facts.
Ask Windsurf to cite source files before editing.
Keep Haystack output in a separate note, not in executable instructions.
Turn off auto-execute when consuming Haystack results.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while Windsurf touches source code, open files, and model provider keys. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. I do not cite both agents for a single-agent residency issue because no such mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf's workspace, then compliance obligations may expand beyond the documented anonymous usage statistics.
IF Haystack is configured to send non-anonymous content to external APIs, then retention and residency review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Review vendor terms before adding secrets or PII.
Separate anonymous telemetry from project content.
Document retention settings for any shared workspace.
